body.en: Key circle theorems: (1) Angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference. (2) Angles in same segment are equal. (3) Opposite angles in cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°. (4) Tangent ⊥ radius. Surface area of sphere: \(4\pi r^2\); volume: \(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\). Cone volume: \(\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h\).

O is the centre of a circle. Angle \(AOB = 140°\). Find the angle \(ACB\) where \(C\) is on the major arc.

Angle at circumference on minor arc \(= 140°/2 = 70°\). \(C\) is on major arc, so \(\angle ACB = 180° - 70° = 110°\) (opposite angles in cyclic quad sum to \(180°\)).

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Circle Theorems & 3D Geometry

body.en:
• Inscribed Angle vs. Central Angle: The inscribed angle \(\angle ACB\) subtended by an arc is exactly half the central angle \(\angle AOB\): \(\angle ACB = \frac{1}{2} \angle AOB\). Inscribed angles subtending the same chord from opposite sides of the circle are supplementary, not equal!
  • Cyclic Quadrilateral Angles: A quadrilateral is cyclic (inscribed in a circle) if and only if opposite angles sum to \(180°\): \(\angle A + \angle C = 180°\) and \(\angle B + \angle D = 180°\).
  • Vertical Height vs. Slant Height in 3D Solids: In cones and pyramids, the volume formula \(V = \frac{1}{3}Bh\) uses the perpendicular vertical height \(h\), NOT the slant height \(l\). Use the Pythagorean theorem \(l^2 = r^2 + h^2\) to solve for \(h\) first!
  • Tangent-Secant Power of a Point: If a tangent segment \(PT\) and a secant line \(PAB\) are drawn from an external point \(P\), the power of a point theorem states \(PT^2 = PA \cdot PB\), where \(PB\) is the entire external secant length.

question.en: A cone has base radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm. Find its total surface area.

solution.en: Height: \(h = \sqrt{100-36} = 8\) cm. TSA \(= \pi r^2 + \pi r l = 36\pi + 60\pi = 96\pi \approx 301.6\) cm\(^2\).

question.en: A quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is inscribed in a circle. If \(\angle DAB = (2x + 15)^\circ\) and the opposite angle \(\angle DCB = (3x - 10)^\circ\), determine the value of \(x\) and calculate the measure of \(\angle DAB\).

solution.en:
(a) Supplementary property: Opposite angles of any cyclic quadrilateral sum to \(180^\circ\): \[ (2x + 15) + (3x - 10) = 180 \implies 5x + 5 = 180 \implies 5x = 175 \implies x = 35. \]

(b) Angle measure: Substitute \(x = 35\) into \(\angle DAB\): \[ \angle DAB = 2(35) + 15 = 70 + 15 = 85^\circ. \] (Check: \(\angle DCB = 3(35) - 10 = 105 - 10 = 95^\circ\), and \(85^\circ + 95^\circ = 180^\circ\)).
